workflow_runs.display_title: [Backport 5.x] test: do not assert a HEAD response body through inject()

head_commit.message:
test: do not assert a HEAD response body through inject() (#7148)

Two tests read the body of a HEAD response through `fastify.inject()`:

- "Should allow registering a constrained GET route after a constrained
HEAD route" (`test/constrained-routes.test.js`) checks `res.payload ===
'custom HEAD response'`;
- "fastify.all should add all the methods to the same url"
(`test/internals/all.test.js`) parses the HEAD payload as JSON.

A real server sends no body for HEAD, and fastify/light-my-request#408
makes `inject()` do the same. @gurgunday approved the behaviour there
but asked for fastify core to be updated before it ships, since these
two tests would fail with it.

These tests now check the response headers instead of the body:

- The constrained route test asserts the `content-type` set by the
custom HEAD handler (`text/plain`) and the `content-length` of `'custom
HEAD response'`. That still shows the custom handler ran, not a HEAD
route derived from the GET one.
- The `fastify.all` test asserts the HEAD response's `content-length`
matches `JSON.stringify({ method: 'HEAD' })` and parses the body only
for the other methods.

Both files pass with the current light-my-request release and with the
#408 branch symlinked into `node_modules` (26 tests each time), so this
can land before or after it. ESLint is clean on both files.

(cherry picked from commit 78d68b2225baa3b7e05ebb5522239f40a4bcf6e8)

head_commit.message:
fix(types): add logSerializers to RouteShorthandOptions

The runtime accepts logSerializers as a per-route option
(lib/route.js) and it is documented under the shared options in
docs/Reference/Routes.md, but RouteShorthandOptions did not include
it. The serializers are passed as pino child logger bindings, so the
return type is widened to match pino serializer semantics: serializer
functions may return objects as well as strings.

(cherry picked from commit 5c1f3935e43b35679c71ea7a65275a348d1efbd1)

### Description

`fastify.addresses()` can return socket path strings when Fastify is
listening on an IPC socket path, but the TypeScript declaration
currently only allows `AddressInfo[]`.

This updates the `addresses()` return type to match the existing runtime
behavior, which is already covered by runtime tests for Unix socket
paths and Windows named pipes.

### Changes proposed:

- Updated `FastifyInstance#addresses()` to return `Array<AddressInfo |
string>`
- Updated the existing type assertion for `addresses()`

2. Ran `npm test`

head_commit.message:
feat!: fail closed when a response content type is not declared in the content map

When a route declares a per-media-type (`content`) response schema but the
response `Content-Type` is neither a declared key nor `*/*`, the payload was
previously serialized with a raw `JSON.stringify`. That fallback bypassed the
response schema and could expose fields the schema was meant to strip.

The route response path now fails closed. If the response content type is not
declared and no `*/*` catch-all matches, `getSchemaSerializer` throws
`FST_ERR_MISSING_CONTENTTYPE_SERIALIZATION_FN` and the reply is a `500`,
surfacing the misconfiguration instead of silently returning unsanitized data.

The error handler call path is unchanged: it still resolves the default error
serializer (requesting `failClosed: false`), so error responses are unaffected.

workflow_runs.display_title: test: pin async hook halt behaviour with 2+ async onSend hooks

head_commit.message:
test: pin async hook halt behaviour with 2+ async onSend hooks

Replying from an async `preHandler` halts the hook chain as documented
with zero or one async `onSend` hooks registered, but not with two or
more: the handler runs and overwrites the status code of a reply that
has already been sent, producing a response whose status and body come
from different places.

The existing sibling test registers a single `onSend` hook, so the
boundary is currently uncovered.

Marked `todo` deliberately. The intended semantics are still open in
 #7090 - whether the documented halt is the contract and the hook count
is irrelevant, or whether sending without `return reply` from an async
hook is unsupported. This commit asserts neither; it only stops the
discrepancy from living solely in an issue, so whoever picks it up
starts from a red test instead of re-deriving the conditions.

Suite result is unchanged: fail 0, todo 1.

Refs: https://github.com/fastify/fastify/issues/7090

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
fix(decorators): handle empty names in existence checks

An empty string is accepted by decorate(), decorateRequest() and
decorateReply(), but truthiness checks treat it as an omitted name.
Dependency checks then take the single-argument overload and throw
a raw TypeError. Request and reply existence checks also skip props.

Check for undefined instead of a falsey name in these paths. Add
public regressions for instance dependencies and request/reply
lookup, dependencies and getDecorator access during injection.

Validation: all 55 decorator tests pass. ESLint and whitespace checks pass.

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(decorators): evaluate instance getters once in getDecorator

head_commit.message:
fix(decorators): evaluate instance getters once

getDecorator reads this[name] once to check its type and again to
return or bind it. An accessor therefore runs twice and can return
a different value from the one that was checked.

Cache the value before checking its type, matching the existing
request and reply implementations. Preserve function binding to
the Fastify instance. Add accessor tests for scalar and function
values, including the number of getter calls.

Validation: all 54 decorator tests pass. ESLint and whitespace
checks pass.

workflow_runs.display_title: fix: contain synchronous throws from custom content type parsers

head_commit.message:
fix: contain synchronous throws from custom content type parsers

A custom parser registered with addContentTypeParser that throws
synchronously crashed the process with an uncaughtException, in both
stream mode and parseAs string/buffer mode, because parser.fn() was
called without a try/catch and only a returned promise rejection was
routed to done(). The same throw from a route handler or a hook is
contained and turned into a 500, so this was an inconsistency across
user-callback boundaries rather than intended behaviour.

Wrap both parser.fn() call sites in try/catch and route a thrown error
to done(error), mirroring the hook runner and preHandlerCallbackInner.
A thrown error with a statusCode is preserved.

head_commit.message:
fix(reply): send stream trailers after the stream actually finishes (#6953)

## Checklist

- [x] run `npm run test`
- [x] tests are included
- [ ] documentation is changed or added
- [x] commit message and code follows the [Developer's Certification of
Origin](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#developers-certificate-of-origin-11)
and the [Code of
conduct](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

## What this does

When trailers are registered, `sendStream()` pipes with `{ end: false }`
so `sendTrailer()` can own `res.end()` once the trailers resolve, since
the default pipe behavior would end the response on its own and race the
trailer flush (`fastify.inject()` never touches a real socket, so this
race never showed up in the existing tests).

The trailer flush itself was wired through a plain `payload.on('end',
...)` listener. If the stream had already ended before `reply.send()`
was called, that `end` event had already fired and the listener was
registered too late, so the trailers never got sent, and since nothing
else was calling `res.end()` either, the response hung.

This moves the trailer flush into the `eos` (`stream.finished`) listener
already present in `sendStream()`. It fires exactly once when the stream
is done, error or not, and it fires even for a stream that finished
before the listener was attached, so the pre-ended case is handled the
same way as the normal one.

## Tests

Added real-socket coverage in `test/reply-trailers.test.js`, since
`inject()` can't see the pipe/`res.end()` race: trailers on a Readable
stream, trailers on a web ReadableStream, a stream with no trailers
registered, a stream that errors before ending, and a stream that has
already ended before being handed to `send()`.

---------

Co-authored-by: Matteo Collina <hello@matteocollina.com>
(cherry picked from commit a479a7ce59f99b6f5a0d20f0745dbd16a3906c09)

head_commit.message:
fix: reap keep-alive connections that become idle after close()

server.close() only reaps the keep-alive connections that are idle when
it is called. A connection that is serving a request at that point
becomes idle once the response is sent, and nothing reaps it, so close()
waits for keepAliveTimeout (72 seconds by default) before resolving.

With forceCloseConnections set to 'idle', call closeIdleConnections()
periodically until server.close() completes, as recommended by Node.js
in test-http-server-close-idle-wait-response.js. The 'false' and 'true'
modes are unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Mbabhazi <samuelmbabhazi@gmail.com>

workflow_runs.display_title: feat: add routerOptions.compile to use find-my-way compiler mode

head_commit.message:
feat: add routerOptions.compile to use find-my-way compiler mode

Bump find-my-way to ^9.10.0 and add a `routerOptions.compile` option
(default `false`). When enabled, the router trees are compiled into
generated JavaScript on preReady, once all the routes are registered,
which makes route lookups 1.3x to 2x faster.

The routing function no longer binds `router.lookup` eagerly, because
`router.compile()` replaces it on the instance.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
